**Short version.** The three rewritten passages are below. Ten project terms still need a definition that the passages do not supply. Seven replaced phrases and eight added definitions need a check against your meaning.

## Passage 1

```markdown
- Block save handles a run of up to 16 consecutive tokens inside one 16-token block.
  - It transposes the K rows of the run in registers.
  - It writes them as whole 64-byte lines, with one store per line.
  - When the run does not fill the block, the store is masked (it writes only selected elements).
  - Every decode step produces a run of one token. Such a run keeps the scatter (a store that writes elements to separate addresses).
- The main thread and the idle main helper threads share the blocks. Each thread claims its blocks from one shared counter.
  - The generated plugin decides the helper count for each pass. The count is not fixed. The traced runs used 7 helpers at tp2.
  - Single-worker callers (the handwritten plugins, the unit tests) and passes of at most 16 tokens store on the calling thread.
```

## Passage 2

```markdown
Where write does worse instead. Write keeps less than read in two kinds of row:

- two writers in one DSU (DynamIQ Shared Unit, Arm's per-cluster shared block) at 160 KiB
- eight writers at any size

In these rows the writers share one path. Write streams run at 32 GB/s, and read streams run at 9 to 12 GB/s. So the write streams reach the limit of the shared path sooner.

The shared path is one of these:

- the mesh port of one DSU (its link to the chip's mesh interconnect)
- the DRAM write limit (section 8)
```

## Passage 3

```markdown
Codex (the OpenAI coding agent) gave this closing assessment. The plan now states it.

The rows can show four things:

- whether the gain needs the prefetchers (hardware that fetches data before the core asks)
- whether the prefetchers aim at the L3 (the level-3 cache)
- whether demand reads (reads the core itself requests) find their cache lines in the L3
- whether more requests wait at the home nodes

The rows alone cannot separate two explanations:

- In your explanation, the data waits in the L3 before the core reads it.
- In the alternative, the DSU handles the same prefetch requests faster.

The external-fetch count with the L3 enabled stays Insufficient data. It stays so until a counter's source and population are established on the target.

The bit-6 boot is the only proposed intervention that directly changes what your explanation describes.
```

## Terms still undefined

The passages do not give the meaning of these terms, so I did not write a definition for them. Each needs one clause at first use.

- Passage 1: K rows, main helper threads, generated plugin, handwritten plugins, tp2
- Passage 2: "keeps" (the quantity that write and read keep is not stated)
- Passage 3: "the rows", home nodes, external-fetch count, bit-6 boot

## Check these against your meaning

I added eight definitions from general knowledge, not from your project:

- Passage 1: masked, scatter
- Passage 2: DSU, mesh port
- Passage 3: Codex, prefetchers, L3, demand reads

- In passage 3, the middle item of the list was split, so the list has four items.
